text:
harper: NimbusAI (acct 3301) flagged April billing. They received two invoices with same base id but different totals. One invoice is missing the promotional discount line so it charged full amount. Customer says they were billed twice for the same period.
leo: can you drop the invoice ids?
harper: INV-2026-0408 and INV-2026-0408-R1. R1 has discount line; the first one does not.
amira: @billing-bot show run 2026-04-08-3301 and any promo flags applied.
billing-bot: invoice-run 2026-04-08-3301 started 2026-04-08T01:05Z finished with warnings. Warnings: [promo_apply:race_condition], [pdf_dispatch:duplicate_send]. Promo state toggled during job window: promo_id=SPRINGPROMO active=true -> false at 2026-04-08T01:06:12Z.
leo: oh. we ran a pricing experiment toggle during billing run window. That explains why two renderings were produced. The first run picked up promo=false (no discount), second run picked up promo=true (discount).
harper: customer says they were charged the higher amount (no discount) and portal shows only the discounted invoice. So their statement has the higher charge and portal is confusing. They want corrected paperwork and either refund or invoice matching the charge.
amira: plan: 1) freeze account 3301 to stop further regenerations; 2) identify which invoice id is associated with payment capture; 3) regen canonical invoice using the promo state at capture time (or if capture matched non-discounted amount, issue invoice to match charge).
product-ops: tagging us - we should never toggle pricing experiments during billing windows. We'll add blackout windows.
billing-bot: payment capture trace: pay_f1a2 amount_cents=1250000 attached to INV-2026-0408 (no suffix). Portal invoice record overwritten by later publish with discount line.
leo: so payment matches the non-discounted invoice. We must not retroactively change portal to show a different total. Action: mark the published portal record immutable if payment exists, void the later reissued invoice, and create a correction invoice INV-2026-0408-CAP that matches the captured amount, leaving charge intact.
finance-bot: created provisional credit memo CM-2026-1010 for acct 3301 in case customer wants refund. Status: pending. Approver: leo.
harper: customer prefers invoice that matches charge. They asked for a signed correction and short explanation why two PDFs arrived.
amira: I'll run a regen in dry-run with publish=false using the canonical promo state tied to capture timestamp and post the CSV.
billing-bot: dry-run regen 2026-04-08-3301-rr complete: canonical_total_cents=1250000, discount_line absent.
leo: good. finance: approve final steps: void INV-2026-0408-R1, issue INV-2026-0408-CAP (matches capture), attach signed note: "A pricing experiment toggle occurred during invoice generation which produced two versions; we have aligned your portal invoice with the captured payment and voided the duplicate." Approve credit memo only if customer requests refund.
finance-bot: approved action. CM-2026-1010 will remain pending.
product-ops: creating blackout policy ticket and sending ops advisory to avoid toggles during billing windows. Also adding a safeguard: pricing toggles must not mutate historical billing state for running jobs.
harper: sent corrected invoice INV-2026-0408-CAP to customer and updated portal with void notice on R1. Customer confirmed receipt and asked for the advisory; forwarded product-ops notice.
leo: root cause summary: live pricing experiment toggle raced with invoice render window -> produced inconsistent renders -> later publish overwrote portal despite payment capture. Mitigations: billing blackout windows, publish immutability after capture, and experiment gate to block changes to price schema during billing runs.
amira: adding regression test to simulate promo toggles during run to ensure billing stability.
harper: closing loop - customer satisfied. Will file for reimbursement of any emergency credit if requested. :white_check_mark:
